entry.gloss: the distance in pitch between two notes
entry.def: The distance in pitch between two notes. An interval is named by its number, counted in letter names, and its quality: C up to E is a major third.

entry.gloss: two notes sounded one after the other
entry.def: An interval between two notes played one after the other, as in a melody.

entry.gloss: two notes sounded together
entry.def: An interval between two notes played at the same time.

entry.gloss: interval size counted in letter names
entry.def: The size of an interval found by counting letter names from the lower note to the upper, both included: C–E is a third (C, D, E). Accidentals do not change the number: C–Eb and C#–E are thirds too. Also called the generic interval.

entry.gloss: perfect, major, minor, augmented or diminished
entry.def: The word that, together with the number, gives an interval's exact size in half steps: perfect, major, minor, augmented or diminished.

entry.gloss: quality of unisons, fourths, fifths and octaves
entry.def: The quality of the unison, fourth, fifth and octave in the sizes found above the tonic of a major scale. These intervals have no major or minor form: made a half step larger they are augmented, a half step smaller diminished.

entry.gloss: second, third, sixth or seventh as in the major scale
entry.def: The quality of a second, third, sixth or seventh in the size found above the tonic of a major scale, such as C–E. Made a half step smaller, without changing the letters, it becomes minor.

entry.gloss: a major interval made a half step smaller
entry.def: A second, third, sixth or seventh one half step smaller than major, with the same letter names: C–E is a major third and C–Eb a minor third.

entry.gloss: a perfect or major interval made a half step larger
entry.def: An interval one half step larger than perfect or major, with the same letter names: C–F# is an augmented fourth and F–G# an augmented second.

entry.gloss: a perfect or minor interval made a half step smaller
entry.def: An interval one half step smaller than perfect or minor, with the same letter names: C–Gb is a diminished fifth and C#–Bb a diminished seventh.

entry.gloss: two notes at the same pitch
entry.def: Two notes at the same pitch with the same letter name; as an interval, the perfect unison. Playing or singing in unison means performing the same notes together.

entry.gloss: a second of one half step
entry.def: The interval of one half step between neighboring letter names, such as E–F, B–C or C–Db; the diatonic half step. It inverts to a major seventh.

entry.gloss: a second of two half steps
entry.def: The interval of two half steps, a whole step, between neighboring letter names, such as C–D or E–F#. It inverts to a minor seventh.

entry.gloss: a third of three half steps
entry.def: A third of three half steps, such as C–Eb or A–C. It is the lower third of a minor triad and inverts to a major sixth.

entry.gloss: a third of four half steps
entry.def: A third of four half steps, two whole steps, such as C–E or F–A. It is the lower third of a major triad and inverts to a minor sixth.

entry.gloss: a fourth of five half steps
entry.def: A fourth of five half steps, such as C–F or G–C. It inverts to a perfect fifth.

entry.gloss: a fourth of six half steps
entry.def: A perfect fourth made a half step larger, such as C–F# or F–B: six half steps, a tritone. It is enharmonic with the diminished fifth, its inversion.

entry.gloss: an interval of three whole steps
entry.def: An interval of three whole steps, six half steps: an augmented fourth or its enharmonic equivalent, the diminished fifth. In a major key it lies between the fourth and seventh degrees, such as F and B in C major.

entry.gloss: a fifth of six half steps
entry.def: A perfect fifth made a half step smaller, such as C–Gb or B–F: six half steps, a tritone. It is the fifth of a diminished triad and inverts to an augmented fourth.

entry.gloss: a fifth of seven half steps
entry.def: A fifth of seven half steps, such as C–G or D–A. It is the fifth of major and minor triads, separates neighboring keys on the circle of fifths, and inverts to a perfect fourth.

entry.gloss: a sixth of eight half steps
entry.def: A sixth of eight half steps, such as C–Ab or E–C. It inverts to a major third.

entry.gloss: a sixth of nine half steps
entry.def: A sixth of nine half steps, such as C–A or F–D. It inverts to a minor third.

entry.gloss: a seventh of ten half steps
entry.def: A seventh of ten half steps, a whole step less than an octave, such as C–Bb or G–F. It inverts to a major second.

entry.gloss: a seventh of eleven half steps
entry.def: A seventh of eleven half steps, a half step less than an octave, such as C–B or F–E. It inverts to a minor second.

entry.gloss: an interval turned upside down
entry.def: Turning an interval upside down by moving its lower note up an octave, or its upper note down. The numbers of an interval and its inversion add up to nine; major becomes minor and augmented diminished, and the reverse, while perfect stays perfect: a major third inverts to a minor sixth. Chords are inverted too: see first inversion.

figure.caption: The major third C–E inverts to the minor sixth E–C.

entry.gloss: an interval larger than an octave
entry.def: An interval larger than an octave, such as a ninth: an octave plus a second. It has the same quality as the simple interval an octave smaller, so C4–D5 is a major ninth. Intervals of an octave or less are called simple.

entry.gloss: an interval or chord that sounds stable
entry.def: An interval or chord that sounds stable and needs no resolution. The consonant intervals are the perfect unison, fifth and octave and the major and minor thirds and sixths; the perfect fourth is consonant between upper voices but dissonant when its lower note is the bass, the lowest sounding note.

entry.gloss: an interval or chord that sounds tense
entry.def: An interval or chord that sounds unstable or tense and traditionally resolves to a consonance. Seconds, sevenths and all augmented and diminished intervals are dissonant, even those that sound the same as a consonance, and so is a perfect fourth whose lower note is the bass.

entry.gloss: melodic move to the next letter name
entry.def: In a melody, a move from one note to a note with the next letter name, up or down: an interval of a second, either a half step or a whole step. Melodies that move mostly by step are called conjunct.

entry.gloss: melodic move larger than a second
entry.def: In a melody, a move larger than a second. Some books call a third a skip and keep the word leap for a fourth or larger. Melodies that move mostly by leap are called disjunct.
